name: Contoso mixed incident
description: All chaos toggles enabled to create a blended client, data model, host, and SQL issue.

report.customerImpact: Customers are experiencing degraded catalogue and checkout performance (p99 3200ms, checkout success 62%).
evidence: Client-side p99 latency: 3200ms vs server-side Cosmos latency: 20ms — 3180ms gap indicates client/SDK or host overhead
Cosmos DB 429 RateLimitExceeded: 55 in last 5 min on products container
Hot partition pattern active: all writes routing to fixed partition key 'hot-category'
Multiple CosmosClient instances: new client created per request instead of singleton
Per-request metadata reads: container properties re-fetched on every operation
Cross-partition fan-out query: SELECT * FROM c without partition key filter
Large document writes: ~52KB documents (recommended <1KB for typical catalogue items)
Unindexed query on ProductsNoIndex: full scan, high RU expected
Query used instead of ReadItem: SELECT * FROM c WHERE c.id=@id vs ReadItemAsync(id,pk)
Host CPU: 85% — CPU burn path active (fibonacci loop on request path)
SQL query latency: 3200ms — artificial slow query path enabled
SQL connection pool pressure: connections held beyond normal release
Recent deployment/change event detected — correlates with incident start
High RU consumption: 1600 RU/min — 16x above healthy baseline
Azure Cosmos DB server-side latency: 20ms — within normal range, indicating service is healthy
ruledOutCauses: Azure Cosmos DB service-side outage ruled out: server-side p99 20ms is healthy
missingEvidence: No packet capture or client network trace collected yet
No query plan capture attached for Cosmos or SQL request path
immediateSafeActions: Disable hot partition chaos toggle — restore natural partition key routing by categoryId/userId
Stop creating new CosmosClient per request — use singleton initialized at startup
Remove per-request metadata reads — cache container properties at startup
Disable CPU burn path — remove synchronous Fibonacci computation from request path
Replace cross-partition query with targeted query using WHERE c.categoryId = @categoryId
Restore indexing policy on ProductsNoIndex, or route queries back to indexed Products container
Replace query with ReadItemAsync(id, partitionKey) for known id+pk combinations
Reduce document size — extract large blobs to Azure Blob Storage, keep documents <1KB
Disable SQL slow query simulation — verify no N+1 query patterns in checkout path
Disable SQL connection pressure — ensure connections returned to pool promptly
Verify singleton CosmosClient initialized at application startup and reused across all requests
Verify SQL connection pool max size is appropriate for expected concurrency
approvalRequiredActions: Re-enable indexing policy on ProductsNoIndex container — requires change request, impacts write RU
Scale AKS node pool — temporary mitigation pending root cause resolution and cost review
Increase Cosmos DB throughput/autoscale — temporary mitigation only; pending cost/risk review
Add SQL index — requires query plan review and DBA approval in production-like environment
doNotDoGuidance: DO NOT treat this as Azure/Cosmos DB service outage — server-side metrics are healthy
DO NOT blindly increase provisioned RU/s — this masks the hot partition root cause
DO NOT ignore hot partition evidence — increasing throughput without fixing key distribution does not resolve root cause
DO NOT leave demo chaos toggles enabled — reset before any customer handoff
report.escalationRecommendation: Do NOT escalate to Azure/Cosmos support. Evidence strongly indicates application-side patterns. Escalate only if server-side latency exceeds 200ms p99, availability drops below 99.9%, or Azure Service Health shows regional impact.
report.temporaryMitigation: Execute the following safe mitigations first: Disable hot partition chaos toggle — restore natural partition key routing by categoryId/userId; Stop creating new CosmosClient per request — use singleton initialized at startup; Remove per-request metadata reads — cache container properties at startup.
report.permanentFix: Refactor Cosmos access patterns to use a singleton client, targeted point reads, well-distributed partition keys, and lean document shapes.
report.rollbackGuidance: Rollback guidance: if approved changes are applied, revert the indexing policy change, reset AKS node scaling to baseline, roll back any Cosmos throughput increase, and remove non-essential SQL indexes after confirming the incident has cleared. For code fixes, disable the corresponding chaos path and redeploy the last known-good build.
verificationCriteria: p99 end-to-end latency returns to <200ms baseline
Zero Cosmos DB 429 errors in 5-minute validation window
CosmosClient singleton verified — one instance at application startup
Unindexed query RU improves after indexing policy restored
Checkout order write succeeds in Azure SQL in <200ms
report.executiveSummary: During the incident window, Contoso Retail customers experienced degraded checkout and product catalogue performance (p99: 3200ms). Investigation evidence indicates the root cause is application-side, specifically: Client-side p99 latency: 3200ms vs server-side Cosmos latency: 20ms — 3180ms gap indicates client/SDK or host overhead; Cosmos DB 429 RateLimitExceeded: 55 in last 5 min on products container; Hot partition pattern active: all writes routing to fixed partition key 'hot-category'. Azure Cosmos DB service-side health remained nominal (server-side latency: 20ms). Azure SQL requires further validation. Immediate corrective actions are identified and safe to execute without service escalation.
report.engineeringRca: Telemetry shows p99 latency at 3200ms with 55 Cosmos 429 events, 1600 RU/min consumption, host CPU 85%, and SQL latency 3200ms. The active toggles (hotPartition, metadataThrottling, multipleClients, highCpu, crossPartitionQuery, largeDocument, missingIndexing, pointReadMisuse, sqlSlowQuery, sqlConnectionPressure) directly align with the observed failure signature. The client-to-server latency delta of 3180ms indicates most latency is introduced in the application, SDK, query design, or host execution path rather than inside the Azure Cosmos DB service plane.
